finding.description: The validator contains Korean source literals without a UTF-8 BOM. Under the documented en-US Windows PowerShell5.1 default CP1252 decoding, a continuation byte in the Korean working-directory literal becomes a smart single quote and changes the parser token stream.
finding.conclusion: The existing PowerShell7 CI does not establish that this script can be launched by the default WindowsPowerShell5.1 installation on an en-US clean Windows client.
finding.suggested_fix: Deliver the non-ASCII script as UTF-8 with BOM, or use ASCII-only source with explicit Unicode string construction, then verify the intended WindowsPowerShell5.1 path.
not_claimed: This is not a Windows5.1 interpreter run.
This is not a clean Windows11 installation test.

official_documentation.supports: Windows PowerShell5.1 and earlier on en-US default to Windows-1252 input for scripts without BOM.
Non-ASCII UTF8NoBOM scripts can break in Windows PowerShell; UTF-8 with BOM is the documented interoperability option.
